reply_text:
The solve loop's stall limit is now 10 (625556d7), so a problem stops after 10 attempts without a new low in its `sorry` count. It takes effect the next time you start the loop.

This run had one case where 10 would have cost something. m03J05 went 17 attempts before its first drop and is now down to 1 `sorry`. It keeps its partial file and gets a fresh 10 attempts next run, so the lower limit shouldn't cost it much. Whatever stops after 10 should be close to your list of hard problems. Those can go to a fresh Codex seat for a new route, as the three topology problems did tonight.

**Why no topology problem closed.** topo2 spent the window on projective-plane chart infrastructure, which doesn't close a problem until a consumer uses it. topo1's first three refill rows all came back "revise", and its three re-routed problems hadn't reached the front of its queue yet. The two routes whose tests compiled first time, t91J06 and t95J02, are the most likely closures when it restarts.
